title: Screen 3: Trigger (entry timing)
description: evaluate_trigger() in app/signals/triple_screen.py: has price resumed direction (close crosses prior day's high/low) using the daily-bar approximation documented in Analyse.md §2, since this is an EOD app rather than intraday.

checklist.step: Confirm daily-bar approximation (close > prior high for bullish trigger, close < prior low for bearish) is still the intended approach — Analyse.md §9 flags intraday-vs-EOD as an open decision, verify it wasn't silently resolved elsewhere first
Implement the trigger check for both tide directions
Return the shape expected by the API (screens.trigger.fired, screens.trigger.reference) per docs/architecture/API.md
Write unit tests covering fired=true and fired=false cases for both directions
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: Confirmed the daily-bar EOD approximation from docs/Analyse.md §2 (bullish trigger: today's close strictly greater than yesterday's high; bearish trigger: today's close strictly less than yesterday's low) as the intended, still-current approach for evaluate_trigger(), and implemented it as such. evaluate_trigger(daily_ohlcv, tide) now returns the exact docs/architecture/API.md `screens.trigger` shape, `{"fired": bool, "reference": str}`, instead of the stub's plain bool. `reference` is set to `close_above_prior_high` / `close_below_prior_low` per the tide direction being evaluated (matching API.md's own example value), or `not_applicable` when the tide is NEUTRAL (no directional rule applies) or there are fewer than two daily bars to compare (no prior bar to reference against) — `fired` is False in both of those cases rather than forcing a guess, consistent with evaluate_impulse()'s and evaluate_tide()'s existing insufficient-data handling in this same module.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §2 states this explicitly for a daily-bar app ('no intraday feed required') and §10's open-questions list recommends end-of-day-only evaluation for the MVP given that same approximation — searched the rest of docs/Analyse.md, docs/architecture/*.md, and every existing docs/tasks/*.json decisions array for any later, more specific resolution of §10's open item and found none; no task (including the in-progress-but-unmerged screen1-tide, PR #9) touches Screen 3 or the intraday-vs-EOD question, so nothing silently resolved this one way or the other before now. This confirmation is being recorded as its own decisions entry, not left implicit, because CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule treats a checklist item phrased as 'confirm/decide X' as meriting a record even when the confirmation is 'yes, no change' rather than a new choice. On the reference-value default for the NEUTRAL/insufficient-data case: considered leaving `reference` as an empty string or reusing one of the two rule names arbitrarily, and rejected both — an empty string loses information silently, and reusing a rule name that wasn't actually evaluated would misrepresent which check (if any) ran. `not_applicable` was chosen as an explicit third value naming the actual state (no directional rule applies) without inventing a fired=True fallback or raising, matching the sibling evaluate_impulse()'s precedent of returning a safe non-gating default (BLUE) rather than guessing under insufficient/ambiguous input. Also note (transparency, not a fabrication risk): the task that dispatched this work asserted evaluate_tide() was already 'merged to main now' — verified via `git log origin/main` and reading app/signals/triple_screen.py on origin/main directly that this was incorrect at the time of this work: evaluate_tide() is implemented only on the still-open, unmerged PR #9 (branch task/screen1-tide), and screen1-tide.json's own state is still 'planned' in docs/tasks/index.json. This task's implementation was written against the actual origin/main stub (three raise NotImplementedError functions), with impulse.py used as the reference for this module's established docstring/edge-case conventions instead, since it is the file's only actually-merged, fully implemented sibling function. evaluate_tide/evaluate_wave were left untouched (still raise NotImplementedError) rather than incorporating PR #9's unmerged code, to avoid taking on scope or a merge conflict surface that belongs to screen1-tide/screen2-wave's own tasks.
